agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# Curlie

Curlie is a friendly frontend to curl that provides easier command-line HTTP requests and prettier output formatting.

## Install

Installers and packages are available for many platforms. Check the project releases page for binary packages or use your platform's package manager.

## Usage

Synopsis:

```
curlie [CURL_OPTIONS...] [METHOD] URL [ITEM [ITEM]]
```

When running interactively, curlie provides pretty-printed output for JSON. To force pretty-printed output, pass `--pretty`.

## Examples

Simple GET: see the image in doc/get.png

Custom method, headers and JSON data: see the image in doc/put.png

## Differences with httpie

- Like `curl` but unlike `httpie`, headers are written on `stderr` instead of `stdout`.
- Output is not buffered; formatting is done on the fly so streamed data can be debugged.

cat > /workspace/tests/run_curl_cases.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Compares `executable --curl ...` output against recorded expectations.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
fail=0; n=0
while IFS= read -r line; do
  [ -z "$line" ] && continue
  expected="${line##*|}"
  argstr="${line%|*}"
  IFS='|' read -r -a args <<< "$argstr"
  if [ "$argstr" = "$line" ]; then args=(); fi
  got=$(./executable --curl "${args[@]}" </dev/null 2>/dev/null)
  n=$((n+1))
  if [ "$got" != "$expected" ]; then
    fail=$((fail+1))
    printf 'FAIL: %s\n  expected: %s\n  got:      %s\n' "$argstr" "$expected" "$got"
  fi
done < tests/curl_cases.txt
echo "$n cases, $fail failures"
EOF
chmod +x /workspace/tests/run_curl_cases.sh; cd /workspace; export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin; ./tests/run_curl_cases.sh"}

#!/bin/bash
# Compares `executable --curl ...` output against recorded expectations.

fail=0; n=0

    printf 'FAIL: %s\n  expected: %s\n  got:      %s\n' "$argstr" "$expected" "$got"

done < tests/curl_cases.txt
echo "$n cases, $fail failures"

// buildURL applies the query items and the localhost shortcut to the URL.
func buildURL(u string, query []string) string {
	if len(query) > 0 {
		sep := "?"
		if strings.Contains(u, "?") {
			sep = "&"
		}
		u += sep + strings.Join(query, "&")
	}
	hasScheme := strings.HasPrefix(u, "http:") || strings.HasPrefix(u, "https:")
	if !hasScheme {
		if strings.HasPrefix(u, "//") {
			u = "http:" + u
		} else {
			u = "http://" + u
		}
	}
	fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, u)
	parsed, err := url.Parse(u)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, err)
		return u
	}
	if strings.HasPrefix(parsed.Host, ":") {
		port := parsed.Host[1:]
		if port == "" {
			parsed.Host = "localhost"
		} else {
			parsed.Host = "localhost:" + port
		}
	}
	out := parsed.String()
	if !hasScheme {
		out = strings.TrimPrefix(out, "http://")
	}
	return out
}

func quoteArg(a string) string {
	if strings.Contains(a, " ") {
		return strconv.Quote(a)
	}
	return a
}

func main() {
	var (
		curlOnly bool
		pretty   bool
	)
	r := &request{}

	// First pass: curlie's own flags are removed wherever they appear.
	var args []string
	for _, a := range os.Args[1:] {
		switch a {
		case "--curl":
			curlOnly = true
		case "--pretty":
			pretty = true
		case "-F", "--form":
			r.form = true
		case "-i":
		default:
			args = append(args, a)
		}
	}

	r.parse(args)

	stdinTTY := isTerminal(os.Stdin.Fd())
	stdoutTTY := isTerminal(os.Stdout.Fd())
	stderrTTY := isTerminal(os.Stderr.Fd())

	// Assemble the curl command line.
	var cargs []string
	cargs = append(cargs, r.opts...)
	switch r.method {
	case "":
	case "HEAD":
		cargs = append(cargs, "-I")
	default:
		cargs = append(cargs, "-X", r.method)
	}
	cargs = append(cargs, r.items...)
	if r.hasData {
		b, _ := json.Marshal(r.data)
		cargs = append(cargs, "-d", string(b))
	}
	if r.hasURL {
		cargs = append(cargs, buildURL(r.url, r.query))
	}

	help := hasArg(cargs, "-h") || hasArg(cargs, "--help")
	silent := hasArg(cargs, "-s") || hasArg(cargs, "--silent")
	verbose := hasArg(cargs, "-v") || hasArg(cargs, "--verbose")
	var hasContentType, hasAccept bool
	for i := 0; i+1 < len(cargs); i++ {
		if cargs[i] == "-H" || cargs[i] == "--header" {
			if name, ok := headerName(cargs[i+1]); ok {
				switch name {
				case "content-type":
					hasContentType = true
				case "accept":
					hasAccept = true
				}
			}
		}
	}

	noArgs := len(cargs) == 0
	cargs = append(cargs, "-s", "-S")
	colorOut := pretty || stdoutTTY
	colorErr := pretty || stderrTTY
	if help {
		colorOut, colorErr = false, false
	}

	if !help {
		if colorErr && !silent {
			cargs = append(cargs, "-v")
		}
		hasD := hasArg(cargs, "-d")
		if !hasD && !stdinTTY {
			cargs = append(cargs, "-d@-")
			hasD = true
		}
		if hasD && !hasArg(cargs, "-F") && !hasContentType {
			cargs = append(cargs, "-H", defaultContentType)
		}
	}
	if !hasAccept {
		cargs = append(cargs, "-H", defaultAccept)
	}

	if curlOnly {
		parts := make([]string, 0, len(cargs)+1)
		parts = append(parts, "curl")
		for _, a := range cargs {
			parts = append(parts, quoteArg(a))
		}
		fmt.Println(strings.Join(parts, " "))
		return
	}

	if noArgs {
		// Without any argument, display curl's full help.
		help = true
		colorOut, colorErr = false, false
		cargs = []string{"-h", "all", "-H", defaultAccept}
	}

	// Request body shown in verbose mode.
	var inBuf stdinBuffer
	bodyFunc := func() []byte {
		for i, a := range cargs {
			if a == "-d" {
				if i+1 < len(cargs) {
					return []byte(cargs[i+1])
				}
				return nil
			}
		}
		if hasArg(cargs, "-d@-") {
			return inBuf.Bytes()
		}
		return nil
	}

	cmd := exec.Command("curl", cargs...)
	if stdinTTY {
		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
	} else {
		cmd.Stdin = io.TeeReader(os.Stdin, &inBuf)
	}
